title.zh: 卷464 列傳二百五十一 李端棻 徐致靖子 仁铸 陈宝箴 黄遵宪 曾鉌 杨深秀 杨锐 刘光第 谭嗣同附：唐才常 林旭 康广仁
title.en: Volume 464 Biographies 251: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijingzi, Ren Zhu, Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Ceng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong with: Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, Kang Guangren
title.raw: 卷464 列傳二百五十一 李端棻 徐致靖子 仁铸 陈宝箴 黄遵宪 曾鉌 杨深秀 杨锐 刘光第 谭嗣同附：唐才常 林旭 康广仁

sentences.zh: 李端棻 徐致靖（子仁鑄） 陳寶箴 黃遵憲 曾鉌 楊深秀 楊銳 劉光第 譚嗣同 唐才常 林旭 康廣仁 李端棻 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijing (son Ren Zhu), Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Ceng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, Kang Guangren — Li Duanfen, style name blank, a man of blank place.
translations.idiomatic: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijing (with his son Ren Zhu), Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Ceng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, and Kang Guangren. Li Duanfen, whose style name was Biyuan, came from Guizhu in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，為大學士、尚書所器。

translations.literal: In the second year he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler; he was valued by Grand Secretary Woren and Minister Luo Dunyan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and received an appointment as compiler; Grand Secretary Woren and Minister Luo Dunyan both prized his talent.

sentences.zh: 十年，出督學政。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he went out as educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later he was sent out to serve as educational commissioner for Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 值寇亂後，荒服道亙，前使者試未遍，始一一按臨，文化漸振。

translations.literal: It happened after the rebel turmoil; the remote borderlands had broken communications, and previous commissioners had not been able to hold examinations everywhere; only then did he go out to inspect each place in turn, and culture gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: This came after the Muslim rebellions, when frontier routes were cut and earlier commissioners had not been able to hold examinations throughout the province; Duanfen now toured each district in person, and learning gradually revived.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉御史，以叔父官京尹，迴避，改故官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to censor; because his uncle held the post of metropolitan magistrate, he withdrew on grounds of kinship and returned to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879 he was made a censor, but had to step aside when his uncle Chaoyi became metropolitan magistrate; he then resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 累擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretariat bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Grand Secretariat bachelor.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In 1892 he was transferred to vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 越六年，調倉場。

translations.literal: Six years later he was transferred to the grain depots.
translations.idiomatic: Six years on he was put in charge of the capital grain depots.

sentences.zh: 前後迭司文柄，四為鄉試考官，一為會試副總裁，喜獎拔士類。

translations.literal: Before and after he repeatedly held literary authority, served four times as provincial examiner, once as associate metropolitan examiner, and delighted in promoting men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: He held literary office again and again, served as provincial examiner four times and as associate metropolitan examiner once, and took pleasure in advancing promising scholars.

sentences.zh: 典試，賞才，以從妹妻之，自是頗納議，娓娓道東西邦制度。

translations.literal: When he presided over examinations he admired talent, gave his younger cousin's daughter in marriage to him, and from then on often accepted his counsel, discoursing at length on the institutions of Eastern and Western states.
translations.idiomatic: While examining candidates in Guangdong he recognized Liang Qichao's ability, married him to his cousin's daughter, and thereafter often took his advice, speaking at length on Western and Eastern political systems.

sentences.zh: 維時上書請變法，兼及興學。

translations.literal: At that time Kang Youwei memorialized requesting reform, including also the promotion of learning.
translations.idiomatic: About this time Kang Youwei submitted memorials calling for reform and for the expansion of education.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遂疏請立京師大學，凡各省府、州、縣遍設學堂，分齋講習；

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Duanfen then memorialized requesting the establishment of a metropolitan university, and that schools be set up throughout every province, prefecture, and county with separate halls for instruction;
translations.idiomatic: In 1896 he memorialized to found a university in the capital and to establish schools in every province, prefecture, and county, each with separate halls for study;

sentences.zh: 並建藏書樓、儀器院、譯書局，廣立報館，選派遊歷生。

translations.literal: and also to build libraries, instrument halls, and translation bureaus, broadly establish newspapers, and select and dispatch students to travel abroad.
translations.idiomatic: together with libraries, instrument halls, and translation bureaus, a wider press, and students sent abroad for study.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，密薦及堪大用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he secretly recommended Kang Youwei and Tan Sitong as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 he privately recommended Kang Youwei and Tan Sitong as men of outstanding capacity.

sentences.zh: 又以各衙門則例，語涉紛歧，疏請刪訂，上尤善之，詔趣各長官定限期革前敝。

translations.literal: He also, because the regulations of the various yamen were worded in conflicting ways, memorialized requesting their revision and deletion; the emperor especially approved this and ordered each chief official to set a deadline for abolishing former abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged revision of the contradictory procedural regulations of the ministries; the emperor warmly approved and ordered each department head to set a deadline for clearing away old abuses.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 未幾，等敗，自疏檢舉，詔褫職，戍。

translations.literal: Before long Kang Youwei and the others failed; Duanfen himself memorialized to denounce himself; an edict stripped his office and sent him into exile in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the reform party fell; Duanfen denounced himself in a memorial, was stripped of office, and was banished to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 中道遘疾，留。

translations.literal: On the road he fell ill and was detained at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the journey and was allowed to remain at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，赦歸，主講。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was pardoned and returned, and lectured at the Jingshi Academy in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1901 he was amnestied and returned home to lecture at the Jingshi Academy in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1907.

sentences.zh: 元年，從、京朝官請，復官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, at the request of Yunnan and Guizhou officials at court, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 1909, at the petition of Yunnan and Guizhou officials in the capital, his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 徐致靖（子仁鑄） ，字，人，寄籍。

translations.literal: Xu Zhijing (son Ren Zhu), style name blank, a man of blank place, with registered domicile elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhijing (with his son Ren Zhu), whose style name was Zijing, was a native of Yixing in Jiangsu but was registered at Wanping.

sentences.zh: 二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 父憂服闋，二十三年，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father ended, in the twenty-third year he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's mourning period he was recalled in 1897 to his former post.

sentences.zh: 嘗憂外患日迫，思所以為獻納計。

translations.literal: Zhijing had once worried that foreign peril pressed daily closer and thought how he might offer counsel to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He had long worried over the mounting foreign threat and looked for ways to advise the throne.

sentences.zh: 子，時以編修督學，倡新學，書告舉。

translations.literal: His son Ren Zhu, then serving as compiler supervising Hunan education, advocated new learning and wrote urging Zhijing to recommend Kang Youwei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ren Zhu, then a compiler serving as Hunan educational commissioner and promoting new learning, wrote urging him to recommend Kang Youwei.

sentences.zh: 遂上言：「國是未定，請申乾斷示從違。

translations.literal: Zhijing then submitted: "The national policy is not yet settled; I beg that Your Majesty's decisive judgment be made clear, showing whether to follow or reject."
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing then memorialized: "The nation's course is still unsettled; I beg Your Majesty to declare your firm decision, showing whether reform is to be embraced or rejected."

sentences.zh: 」藉以覘上意。

translations.literal: " — thereby to gauge the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: " — thus to sound out the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔果求通才，於是奏堪大用，並及、等。

translations.literal: Before long an edict indeed sought men of outstanding talent; Zhijing then memorialized that Kang Youwei was fit for great employment, and also named Liang Qichao, Huang Zunxian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict did call for men of talent; he then recommended Kang Youwei as eminently employable, together with Liang Qichao, Huang Zunxian, and others.

sentences.zh: 又連上書請廢製藝，改試策論，省冗官，酌置散卿。

translations.literal: He also submitted successive memorials requesting abolition of the examination essay, changing to policy discourse, reducing redundant officials, and considering the appointment of honorary grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: He followed with further memorials to abolish the eight-legged essay in favor of policy essays, cut redundant offices, and create honorary grand secretary posts.

sentences.zh: 復以邊患棘，宜練重兵，力荐主軍事。

translations.literal: He further, because border troubles were acute, urged that heavy troops be trained and strongly recommended Yuan Shikai to direct military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Citing acute border danger, he urged training a strong army and strongly recommended Yuan Shikai to take charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 上皆然其言，敕依行。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all his proposals and ordered them carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every point and ordered them implemented.

sentences.zh: 罷斥禮部尚書等阻遏言路，遂命權右侍郎。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xu Yingkui and others who blocked the memorial channel were dismissed; Zhijing was then ordered to act as right vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yingkui, minister of Rites, and others who had blocked memorials were removed, and Zhijing was appointed acting right vice minister.

sentences.zh: 二十四年八月，太后復出訓政，參預新政諸臣皆獲罪。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year the empress dowager resumed regency; all who had taken part in the new policies were punished.
translations.idiomatic: In August 1898 the empress dowager resumed rule; every official involved in the reform was punished.

sentences.zh: 褫職坐系，尋定永遠監禁，亦罷官。

translations.literal: Zhijing was stripped of office and imprisoned; soon he was sentenced to perpetual confinement, and Ren Zhu was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing lost his post and was imprisoned, soon sentenced to lifelong detention; Ren Zhu was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 庚子，聯軍陷京師，始出獄待罪，詔赦免。

translations.literal: In the gengzi year, when the allied armies took the capital, he was released from prison to await judgment and was pardoned by edict.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, when the allied armies occupied Beijing, he was released to await judgment and then amnestied.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 陳寶箴 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Chen Baozhen, style name blank, a man of blank place.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baozhen, whose style name was Youming, was a native of Yining in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 少負志節，詩文皆有法度，為所器。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed moral resolution; his poetry and prose both had discipline, and he was valued by Zeng Guofan.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed strong character; his literary work was disciplined, and Zeng Guofan prized him.

sentences.zh: 以舉人隨父治鄉團，禦寇。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he followed his father Wei Lin in organizing local militia to resist the Cantonese rebels.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he joined his father Wei Lin in organizing local defense against the Taiping rebels.

sentences.zh: 已而走，參戎幕，軍、間。

translations.literal: He then went to Hunan and joined Yi Peishen's military staff, campaigning between Laifeng and Longshan.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Hunan, entered Yi Peishen's staff, and campaigned between Laifeng and Longshan.

sentences.zh: 來犯，軍飢疲，走募糧，糧至不絕，守益堅，寇稍稍引去。

translations.literal: When Shi Dakai came to attack, the army was hungry and weary; Baozhen went to Yongshun to raise grain; grain arrived without cease, the defense grew firmer, and the rebels gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai attacked, the troops were starving and exhausted; Baozhen went to Yongshun to raise grain, supplies kept coming, the defense held firm, and the rebels gradually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 之，為畫策殲寇，事寧，敘知府，超授。

translations.literal: Baozhen went to Jiangxi and plotted with Xi Baotian the destruction of the bandit Hong Fuzhen; when the affair was settled he was recorded as prefect and was promoted by exception to Hebei circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi he helped Xi Baotian plan the destruction of Hong Fuzhen; when peace returned he was ranked as prefect and was exceptionally promoted to Hebei circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 創，遴選三州學子，延名師教之。

translations.literal: He founded the Academy of Practical Learning, selected students from three prefectures, and invited famous teachers to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Academy of Practical Learning, chose students from three prefectures, and brought in distinguished teachers.

sentences.zh: 遷按察使，坐事免。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhejiang as surveillance commissioner and was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was made surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang but was later dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 巡撫薦其才，十六年，召入都，除按察使，署布政使。

translations.literal: Hunan governor Wang Wenshao recommended his talent; in the sixteenth year he was summoned to the capital, appointed surveillance commissioner of Hubei, and acted as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan governor Wang Wenshao recommended him; in 1890 he was called to the capital, made surveillance commissioner of Hubei, and acted as provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢直隸布政使，入對，時東戰亟，見上形容憂悴，請日讀，以期變不失常。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to provincial treasurer of Zhili; on audience the Sino-Japanese war was urgent; he saw the emperor's countenance worn with grief and requested daily reading of the Kangxi emperor's Imperially Compiled Changes, so that amid change he might not lose constancy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 he was promoted to Zhili provincial treasurer; at audience the war with Japan was raging; seeing the emperor's haggard face, he urged daily study of the Kangxi emperor's commentary on the Changes so that amid upheaval the ruler might keep his bearings.

sentences.zh: 他所陳奏語甚多，並稱旨。

translations.literal: His other memorial statements were many, and all met with imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: His many other memorials likewise won the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 上以為忠，命治糈台，專摺奏事。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded him as loyal and ordered him to manage the grain depots and handle memorials exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him loyal and put him in charge of the grain depots with sole responsibility for memorials.

sentences.zh: 成，泣曰：「殆不國矣！

translations.literal: When the Treaty of Shimonoseki was concluded, he wept and said: "The state is nearly lost!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Treaty of Shimonoseki was signed, he wept and said, "The state is all but lost!"

sentences.zh: 」 明年，以薦，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: " The next year, on Rong Lu's recommendation, he was promoted to Hunan governor.
translations.idiomatic: " The following year, on Rong Lu's recommendation, he was made governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 撫幕有者，植黨私利，至即重治之。

translations.literal: In the governor's staff there was Ren Lin, who formed factions for private gain; as soon as Baozhen arrived he punished him severely.
translations.idiomatic: A staff member named Ren Lin had built a faction for private profit; Baozhen punished him severely as soon as he took office.

sentences.zh: 布政使為關說，據以上聞，獲譴。

translations.literal: The Zhili provincial treasurer Wang Lian interceded for him; Baozhen reported this upward and Wang was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili treasurer Wang Lian pleaded for Ren; Baozhen reported this to the throne and Wang was punished.

sentences.zh: 覆按被劾事，盡暴其任用非人狀，遂褫職。

translations.literal: On reinvestigation of the impeached affair he fully exposed Nianzu's employment of unfit men, and Nianzu was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Reinvestigating the case, he fully exposed Shi Nianzu's appointment of unworthy men, and Nianzu was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 繇是有伉直聲。

translations.literal: From this he gained a reputation for stern uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby gained a reputation for uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 俗故闇僿，思以一隅致富強，為東南倡，先後設電信，置小輪，建製造槍彈廠，又立保衛局、、。

translations.literal: Hunan custom was formerly benighted and crude; Baozhen thought to make one corner rich and strong as a model for the southeast; he successively set up telegraph lines, installed steam launches, built a factory for manufacturing firearms and ammunition, and also established a Public Security Bureau, the Southern Study Society, and the Current Affairs Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan was backward and insular; he aimed to make the province a model of wealth and strength for the southeast, installing telegraph lines and steam launches, building an arms factory, and founding the Public Security Bureau, the Southern Study Society, and the Current Affairs Academy.

sentences.zh: 延主學，俗大變。

translations.literal: He invited Liang Qichao to direct Hunan learning, and local custom changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in Liang Qichao to direct education in Hunan, and local attitudes changed dramatically.

sentences.zh: 又疏請釐正學術及練兵、籌款諸大端，上皆嘉納，敕令持定見，毋為浮言動，並特旨褒勵之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting correction of scholarship and the great matters of training troops and raising funds; the emperor commended and accepted all, ordered him to hold to his settled views and not be moved by loose talk, and also issued a special edict praising and encouraging him.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on reforming scholarship, training troops, and raising revenue; the emperor approved all points, told him to stand firm against loose talk, and issued a special edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 是時負盛名，司道咸屏息以伺。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Zhidong enjoyed great renown, and all circuit and prefectural officials held their breath to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong then enjoyed enormous prestige, and every provincial official watched him in silence.

sentences.zh: 初綰籓，遇事不合，獨與爭無私撓，雖不懌，無如何也。

translations.literal: When Baozhen first held the Hubei provincial administration, they disagreed on affairs; he alone contended with Zhang without private bias; though Zhang was displeased, he could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen first governed Hubei as treasurer, they often clashed; he alone stood up to Zhang without favoritism; Zhang was displeased but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 久之，兩人深相結，凡條上新政皆聯銜，而撫反不與。

translations.literal: After a long time the two men became deeply allied; whenever they memorialized on the new policies they signed jointly, while Hubei governor Tan Jixun did not join them.
translations.idiomatic: In time the two became close allies and co-signed every memorial on the new policies, while Hubei governor Tan Jixun held aloof.

sentences.zh: 會言事數見效。

translations.literal: It happened that Kang Youwei's proposals several times took effect.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Youwei's proposals were meanwhile winning repeated approval.

sentences.zh: 素慕、薦士，因上言、、、佐新政。

translations.literal: Baozhen had long admired Zeng and Hu in recommending talent; he therefore memorialized that Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu should assist the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: Long admiring Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi as talent-spotters, he recommended Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu to help carry out the reforms.

sentences.zh: 上方詔求通變才，遽擢京卿，參新政，於是四人上書論時事無顧忌。

translations.literal: The court was then issuing edicts seeking men of adaptive talent; the four were abruptly promoted to capital ministers and took part in the new policies; thereupon the four memorialized on current affairs without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was calling for adaptable talent; all four were suddenly promoted to metropolitan ministers to join the reform, and they memorialized on current affairs without restraint.

sentences.zh: 又言四人雖才，恐資望輕，視事過易，原得厚重大臣如者領之。

translations.literal: He also said that though the four had talent, he feared their seniority was light and they might take office too lightly; he wished that a weighty senior such as Zhang Zhidong might lead them.
translations.idiomatic: He added that though talented, the four were junior in standing and might treat office too lightly; he asked that a senior figure such as Zhang Zhidong supervise them.

sentences.zh: 疏上而太后已出訓政，誅四京卿，罪及舉主，去官，其子主事亦革職，並毀學所著、、、諸書。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up the empress dowager had already resumed regency; the four capital ministers were executed; guilt reached the recommender; Baozhen left office, his son Sanli, a director, was also dismissed, and the Hunan school's writings — Study Compact, Definitions, Notes, and Answers — were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial arrived after the empress dowager had resumed rule; the four ministers were executed; the recommender was punished; Baozhen lost office, his son Sanli was dismissed, and Hunan school texts such as Study Compact, Definitions, Notes, and Answers were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 初，已革道員，以張揭帖攻西教為總督所治。

translations.literal: Earlier, the dismissed circuit intendant Zhou Han of Ningxiang had been punished by the governor-general for posting broadsheets attacking Western religion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, dismissed Ningxiang circuit intendant Zhou Han had been punished by the governor-general for posting anti-Christian broadsheets.

sentences.zh: 至，復刊帖傳布，令毀之，毆毀帖者，怒，下之獄。

translations.literal: When Baozhen arrived, Zhou again printed and circulated the posters; Baozhen ordered them destroyed; Zhou beat those who destroyed them; Baozhen in anger had him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen arrived, Zhou printed new posters; Baozhen ordered them destroyed; Zhou beat those who tore them down; Baozhen had him jailed in anger.

sentences.zh: 舊黨恨次骨，然喜新之士，亦以此翕然稱之。

translations.literal: The old faction hated him to the marrow, yet men who favored the new likewise united in praising him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Conservatives hated him bitterly, yet reform-minded men praised him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 既去，諸所營構便於民者，雖效益已著，皆廢毀無一存雲。

translations.literal: After he left, all the institutions he had built for the people's benefit, though their good effects were already evident, were abolished and destroyed without a single one remaining.
translations.idiomatic: After his removal, every institution he had built for the public good, however successful, was dismantled until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy.

sentences.zh: 黃遵憲 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Huang Zunxian, style name blank, a man of blank place.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zunxian, whose style name was Gongdu, was a native of Jiaying prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以舉人入貲為道員。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he purchased office and became a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he bought his way to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 充使參贊，著上之朝。

translations.literal: He served as legation counselor in Japan and presented his Record of Japan to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He served as counselor on the mission to Japan and submitted his Record of Japan to the court.

sentences.zh: 旋移總領事。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to consul-general at San Francisco.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made consul-general at San Francisco.

sentences.zh: 吏嘗藉口衛生，逮僑滿獄。

translations.literal: American officials once used sanitation as a pretext and arrested Chinese sojourners until the jails were full.
translations.idiomatic: American officials once used public health as a pretext to fill the jails with Chinese immigrants.

sentences.zh: 徑詣獄中，令從者度其容積，曰：「此處衛生顧右於僑居邪？

translations.literal: Zunxian went straight to the prison and ordered his attendants to measure its capacity, saying: "Is sanitation here really better than where the sojourners live?"
translations.idiomatic: Zunxian went straight to the jail and had his attendants measure its capacity, saying, "Is this place really more sanitary than where our people live?"

sentences.zh: 」吏謝，遽釋之。

translations.literal: " The American officials apologized and released them at once.
translations.idiomatic: " The officials apologized and released them immediately.

sentences.zh: 歷鹽法道，署按察使。

translations.literal: He served as Chang-Bao salt commissioner and acted as surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Chang-Bao salt commissioner and acted as surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時為巡撫，行新政，首倡民治於眾曰：「亦自治其身，自治其鄉而已。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Baozhen was governor and was carrying out new policies; Zunxian first advocated popular self-government to the crowd, saying: "One need only govern oneself and govern one's own township."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baozhen was then governor and pushing reforms; Zunxian first preached popular self-government, saying, "Begin by governing yourself and your own township."

sentences.zh: 由一鄉推之一縣、一府、一省，以迄全國，可以成共和之郅治，臻大同之盛軌。

translations.literal: From one township extend to one county, one prefecture, one province, and on to the whole country — thus republican government at its best may be achieved and the great path of Great Unity reached.
translations.idiomatic: Extend that from one township to a county, a prefecture, a province, and the whole country, and you can build true republican government and reach the ideal of Great Unity.

sentences.zh: 」於是略仿西國巡警之制，設保衛局，凡與民利民瘼相麗，而為一方民力能舉者，悉屬之，領以民望，而官輔其不及焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon, roughly imitating Western police systems, he established a Public Security Bureau; all matters touching the people's benefit and hardship that local popular strength could undertake were placed under it, led by men of local esteem, while officials assisted where they fell short.
translations.idiomatic: " He then modeled a Public Security Bureau on Western policing: every local matter of public welfare that the people could manage was entrusted to respected local leaders, with officials assisting only where needed.

sentences.zh: 尋解職，奉出使之命，未行而黨禍起，遂罷歸。

translations.literal: Soon he resigned office, received orders to go abroad as envoy, but before he set out the factional disaster arose and he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office, was appointed envoy to Japan, but before he could depart the reform purge struck and he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 著有等。

translations.literal: His writings include Human Realm Studio Poems and others.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote works including Human Realm Studio Poems and others.

sentences.zh: 曾鉌 ，字，氏，正白旗人。

translations.literal: Ceng He, style name blank, of the Xitala clan, a bondservant of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng He, whose style name was Huaiqing, of the Xitala clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父，將軍。

translations.literal: His father Qingyun was general at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingyun was general at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 以任子為工部主事，累遷郎中，充軍機章京，轉御史。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he became a director in the Ministry of Works, was repeatedly promoted to bureau director, served as a Grand Council clerk, and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he entered the Ministry of Works, rose to bureau director, served on the Grand Council staff, and became a censor.

sentences.zh: 九年，出為督糧道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he went out as grain transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1883 he was sent out as Shaanxi grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 、各屬農民納糧例繳省倉，道塗艱遠，多弊竇，設法清釐之，民稱便。

translations.literal: In Xi'an and Tongzhou the peasants of each subordinate district ordinarily paid grain tax into the provincial granary; the roads were hard and long and there were many abuses; he devised methods to clear them up, and the people said it was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Peasants in Xi'an and Tongzhou districts usually paid grain tax at the provincial granary over long, difficult roads with many abuses; he reformed the system, and the people welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 士風樸僿，藝事苦窳，延、主書院，督課實學，士論翕然。

translations.literal: The scholarly style of the capital region was plain and crude, and the arts were painfully poor; he invited Bo Jingwei of Chang'an and Liu Guangzan of Xianyang to direct the Guanzhong Academy, supervised instruction in practical learning, and scholarly opinion united in approval.
translations.idiomatic: Scholarly culture in the capital region was plain and craft skills poor; he brought in Bo Jingwei and Liu Guangzan to run the Guanzhong Academy, stressed practical learning, and won broad approval among scholars.

sentences.zh: 又設蠶桑局，聘織師教以煮湅織染法，歲出絲帛埒、。

translations.literal: He also established a sericulture bureau, hired weaving masters to teach boiling, reeling, weaving, and dyeing, and each year the silk and cloth produced rivaled Qi and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up a sericulture bureau, hired weaving masters to teach full silk processing, and annual output rivaled Shandong and Henan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1887 he was made surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，母憂解職。

translations.literal: The next year, on his mother's death, he left office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，起故官，俄遷布政使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was recalled to his former office and soon was transferred to provincial treasurer of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he resumed office and was soon made Gansu provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，調，迴避，留本任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Zhili but withdrew on grounds of kinship and remained in his present post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 he was transferred to Zhili but stayed in Gansu on kinship grounds.

sentences.zh: 擢巡撫，慨然曰：「時艱至此，猶可拘成法不變耶？

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor of Hubei and said with emotion: "The times are hard to this point — can we still cling to established rules and not change?"
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to governor of Hubei, he exclaimed, "With the times this desperate, how can we still cling to old rules and refuse change?"

sentences.zh: 」於是假總督印上陳補官、掣籤、度支、訟獄四事，宜變通成例，厚植國本。

translations.literal: " Thereupon, using the Shaan-Gan governor-general's seal, he memorialized on four matters — filling offices, drawing lots, fiscal administration, and litigation — urging that established precedents be flexibly changed to strengthen the nation's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: " He then used the Shaan-Gan governor-general's seal to memorialize on appointments, lot-drawing, finance, and litigation, urging flexible reform of precedent to strengthen the state.

sentences.zh: 侍讀學士、光祿寺少卿彈其亂政，詔褫職。

translations.literal: Reader-in-waiting Yigu and vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Zhang Zhongxin impeached him for disordering government, and an edict stripped his office.
translations.idiomatic: Reader-in-waiting Yigu and Zhang Zhongxin of the Court of Imperial Entertainments impeached him for subverting government, and he was dismissed by edict.

sentences.zh: 始，官京朝，家綦貧，僦居陋室。

translations.literal: At first, when Ceng He held office in the capital, his family was extremely poor and he rented a mean dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his capital career his family was desperately poor and he rented a shabby room.

sentences.zh: 及任外台，孜孜民事，不顧問有無。

translations.literal: When he held office in the provinces he worked tirelessly at civil affairs and paid no heed to whether he had means or not.
translations.idiomatic: In provincial office he devoted himself tirelessly to public business, heedless of his own means.

sentences.zh: 既閒廢，出入皆徒步，民恆歲醵金濟之。

translations.literal: After he was idled and dismissed, he went everywhere on foot; the people of Shaanxi regularly collected money each year to support him.
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal he went everywhere on foot; Shaanxi people regularly pooled money to support him.

sentences.zh: 後益困，至敝衣鬻卜都市。

translations.literal: Later he grew still poorer, until in worn-out clothes he sold divination in the marketplaces of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He grew still poorer and eventually sold divination in the capital markets in threadbare clothes.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 改元，總督為奏復原官。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title, Governor-General Duanfang memorialized to restore his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xuantong reign began, Governor-General Duanfang had his former rank restored.

sentences.zh: 楊深秀 ，字，本名，人。

translations.literal: Yang Shenxiu, style name blank, original name Yuxiu, a man of blank place.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shenxiu, whose style name was Yicun and whose original name was Yuxiu, was a native of Wenxi in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 少穎敏，諳西算術。

translations.literal: In youth he was sharp and clever and versed in Chinese and Western mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was quick-witted and versed in both Chinese and Western mathematics.

sentences.zh: 初，以舉人入貲為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: At first, as a provincial graduate he purchased office and became an assistant department director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, as a provincial graduate, he bought his way to assistant director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 假歸，值大饑，銜命籌賑，條上改革差徭法，困少蘇。

translations.literal: On leave he returned home; a great famine occurred; Yan Jingming was ordered to organize relief; Shenxiu submitted proposals to reform the corvée and tax system, and distress eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: On leave during a great famine he was ordered to organize relief under Yan Jingming; he proposed corvée and tax reforms that brought some relief.

sentences.zh: 十五年，成進士，就本官遷郎中，轉御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he passed the jinshi examination, retained his former office and was promoted to bureau director, then transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1889 he became a jinshi, kept his post while rising to bureau director, then became a censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「時勢危迫，不革舊無以圖新，不變法無以圖存。

translations.literal: He once said: "The times are perilously pressing; without reforming the old there is no way to seek the new; without changing the laws there is no way to seek survival."
translations.idiomatic: He once declared, "The times are desperate: without overturning the old order there can be no renewal, and without reform there can be no survival."

sentences.zh: 」 二十四年，人脅割、。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-fourth year the Russians compelled the cession of Port Arthur and Dalian Bay.
translations.idiomatic: " In 1898 Russia forced the cession of Port Arthur and Dalian Bay.

sentences.zh: 深秀力請聯、拒之，詞甚切直。

translations.literal: Shenxiu urgently requested alliance with Britain and Japan to resist them, his language very blunt and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu urgently urged alliance with Britain and Japan to resist, in blunt, forceful language.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷銳意行新政，而大臣恆多異議。

translations.literal: At that time the court was keen to carry out new policies, but grand ministers constantly had many differing opinions.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then eager to pursue reform, but senior ministers constantly dissented.

sentences.zh: 乃與先後疏請定國是，又以取士之法未善，請參酌、、舊制，釐正文體，下其議於禮部，尚書心非之，未奏也。

translations.literal: Shenxiu then with Xu Zhijing successively memorialized requesting settlement of the national policy; he also, because the method of selecting scholars was not good, requested reference to Song, Yuan, and Ming old systems to rectify literary form; the proposal was sent down to the Ministry of Rites; Minister Xu Yingkui disapproved in his heart and did not memorialize upward.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xu Zhijing then memorialized to fix the national course; he also urged reform of the examination essay by drawing on Song, Yuan, and Ming models; the matter went to the Ministry of Rites, but Minister Xu Yingkui withheld the memorial.

sentences.zh: 會議經濟特科務減額，於是合彈其阻撓。

translations.literal: It happened that the special economic examination was discussed with a plan to reduce quotas; Shenxiu then joined Song Bolu in impeaching Xu for obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: When the special economic examination was discussed with plans to cut quotas, he joined Song Bolu in impeaching Xu for obstruction.

sentences.zh: 上令自陳，奏上，劾​​夤緣要津，請罷斥，詞連，上不之詰也。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Xu to explain himself; when his memorial went up he impeached Kang Youwei for currying favor at key posts and requested dismissal, his words implicating Shenxiu; the emperor did not pursue the matter against Shenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Xu to explain; Xu counter-attacked Kang Youwei for currying favor at court and implicated Shenxiu, but the emperor did not pursue Shenxiu.

sentences.zh: 御史劾傳布有為所立，並暴交通內外狀，責以代人報復，反獲咎。

translations.literal: Censor Wen Ti impeached Shenxiu for spreading the Society to Protect the State that Kang Youwei had founded and exposed Kang's communications inside and outside the court; the emperor rebuked Wen for retaliating on another's behalf, and Wen himself was blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wen Ti impeached him for spreading Kang's Society to Protect the State and exposed Kang's court connections; the emperor rebuked Wen for personal vendetta, and Wen was blamed instead.

sentences.zh: 益感奮，連上書請設譯書局，派王公遊歷各國，並定遊學章程，皆報可。

translations.literal: Shenxiu grew still more inspired; he submitted successive memorials requesting establishment of a translation bureau, dispatch of princes and dukes to tour various countries, and fixing regulations for study abroad; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: More fired up than ever, he memorialized for a translation bureau, princely missions abroad, and regulations for study overseas; all were approved.

sentences.zh: 又請試庶官，日番二十人，料簡貞實，而汰其庸愚罷老不諳時務者，繇是廷臣益側目。

translations.literal: He also requested testing of ordinary officials, twenty men each day in rotation, selecting the upright and solid while eliminating the mediocre, foolish, aged, and those unversed in current affairs; from this court ministers increasingly looked askance at him.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed daily testing of ordinary officials, twenty at a time, to promote the capable and weed out the mediocre and out of touch; courtiers watched him with growing hostility.

sentences.zh: 巡撫圖治甚急，中蜚語，為剖辨之，上以特旨褒，乃得行其志。

translations.literal: Hunan governor Chen Baozhen was governing with great urgency; slander reached the center; Shenxiu explained and refuted it; the emperor issued a special edict praising Baozhen, and only then could Baozhen carry out his aims.
translations.idiomatic: When slander reached the court against the urgently reforming Hunan governor Chen Baozhen, Shenxiu defended him; the emperor issued a special commendation, and Baozhen could proceed.

sentences.zh: 八月，政變，舉朝惴惴，懼大誅至，獨抗疏請太后歸政。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the political coup occurred; the whole court was fearful, dreading mass executions; Shenxiu alone submitted a defiant memorial requesting that the empress dowager return power.
translations.idiomatic: In August the coup struck; the court trembled expecting mass executions; Shenxiu alone memorialized demanding the empress dowager restore power to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 方疏未上時，其子苦口諫止，厲聲叱之退。

translations.literal: Just before the memorial went up, his son Futian earnestly admonished him to stop; he shouted him down and ordered him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial went up, his son Futian begged him to stop; he shouted him down and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 俄被逮，論棄市。

translations.literal: Soon he was arrested and sentenced to public execution.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon arrested and sentenced to execution.

sentences.zh: 性鯁直，嘗面折人過，以此叢忌。

translations.literal: His nature was blunt and upright; he once rebuked others' faults to their faces, and for this drew many resentments.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt and upright by nature, he often confronted others with their faults face to face, earning many enemies.

sentences.zh: 官臺諫十閱月，封事二十餘上，稿不具存，惟獄中詩三章流傳於世。

translations.literal: He held censorial office ten months; more than twenty sealed memorials went up; the drafts are not fully preserved; only three poems from prison circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: In ten months as censor he submitted more than twenty sealed memorials; most drafts are lost, but three prison poems survive.

sentences.zh: 著有、。

translations.literal: His writings include Drafts from the Hall of Empty Voices and the New Gazetteer of Wenxi County.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Drafts from the Hall of Empty Voices and the New Gazetteer of Wenxi County.

sentences.zh: 楊銳 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Yang Rui, style name blank, a man of blank place.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rui, whose style name was Shujiao, was a native of Mianzhu in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 少俊慧，督學奇其才，招入幕。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and gifted; educational commissioner Zhang Zhidong marveled at his talent and recruited him into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Clever as a youth, he impressed educational commissioner Zhang Zhidong, who brought him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 肄業，年最少，嘗冠其曹。

translations.literal: He studied at the Zunjing Academy; though youngest in years, he often led his class.
translations.idiomatic: At the Zunjing Academy he was the youngest student yet often topped his class.

sentences.zh: 優貢朝考得知縣。

translations.literal: As an outstanding tribute student he passed the metropolitan examination and received appointment as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: As an outstanding tribute student he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed magistrate.

sentences.zh: 督，從赴。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhidong governed the two Guang provinces, Rui followed him to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang governed Guangdong and Guangxi, Rui followed him south.

sentences.zh: 十一年，舉順天鄉試，考取內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was selected as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and became a Grand Secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，薦應經濟特科。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Zhang recommended him to sit for the special economic examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 Zhang recommended him for the special economic examination.

sentences.zh: 又以薦，與、、並加四品卿，充軍機章京，參新政。

translations.literal: He was also recommended by Chen Baozhen; together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu he was all given fourth-rank minister status, appointed Grand Council clerk, and took part in the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baozhen also recommended him; with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu he was made a fourth-rank minister and Grand Council clerk to join the reforms.

sentences.zh: 召見，面陳興學、練兵為救亡策，稱旨。

translations.literal: On audience Rui stated face to face that promoting learning and training troops were strategies to save the state; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he urged education and military training as the path to national salvation; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 七月，禮部主事上封事，尚書等格不奏。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Ministry of Rites director Wang Zhao submitted a sealed memorial; Ministers Xu Yingkui and others blocked it and did not memorialize upward.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wang Zhao of the Ministry of Rites submitted a sealed memorial; Xu Yingkui and other ministers blocked it from reaching the throne.

sentences.zh: 上聞，震怒，盡褫尚書侍郎六人革職，朝臣皆不自安。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he was greatly angered and stripped all six ministers and vice ministers of office; court officials were all ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and dismissed all six ministers and vice ministers; the court was shaken.

sentences.zh: 上手詔密諭云：「近日朕仰觀聖母意旨，不欲退此老耄昏庸大臣而進英勇通達之人，亦不欲將法盡變。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote a secret edict instructing Rui: "Recently I have observed the empress dowager's intent: she does not wish to remove these aged, muddled, incompetent ministers and advance brave, penetrating men, nor does she wish the laws wholly changed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote Rui a secret instruction: "Lately I see the empress dowager does not want these senile, incompetent ministers removed in favor of bold, capable men, nor does she want the laws wholly changed."

sentences.zh: 朕豈不知積弱不振，非力行新政不可？

translations.literal: How could I not know that long weakness and failure to revive make vigorous new policies indispensable?
translations.idiomatic: Do I not know that only vigorous reform can save a state so long weakened?

sentences.zh: 然此時不惟朕權力所不及，若強行之，朕位且不能保。

translations.literal: Yet at this time not only is it beyond my power; if forced through, even my throne could not be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: But now it is beyond my power; if I forced reform through, I could not even keep my throne.

sentences.zh: 爾與、、等詳悉籌議，必如何而後能進用英達，使新政及時舉行，又不致少拂聖意，即具奏，候朕審擇，不勝焦慮之至！

translations.literal: You and Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, and the rest should deliberate in full detail how talented men may be advanced, new policies carried out in good time, and yet the empress dowager's mind not be even slightly offended; memorialize at once for my examination and choice — I am overcome with anxious distress!"
translations.idiomatic: You, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, and the others must work out how to advance able men, carry out reform in time, and yet not offend the empress dowager; memorialize at once for my decision — I am desperate with anxiety!"

sentences.zh: 」復奏言：「太后親挈大位授之皇上，皇上宜以孝先天下，遇事將順。

translations.literal: " Rui memorialized again: "The empress dowager personally bestowed the great throne upon Your Majesty; Your Majesty should put filial piety before all under Heaven and yield to her in affairs."
translations.idiomatic: " Rui replied: "The empress dowager personally gave you the throne; you should put filial duty first and yield to her in affairs."

sentences.zh: 變法宜有次第，進退大臣不宜太驟。

translations.literal: Reform should have an order of steps; advancing and dismissing great ministers should not be too sudden.
translations.idiomatic: Reform should proceed in stages; ministerial appointments and dismissals should not be rushed.

sentences.zh: 」上是之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 已而太后再訓政，諸言新政者皆予重誅。

translations.literal: Before long the empress dowager resumed regency; all who had spoken for the new policies were given heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the empress dowager resumed rule; every advocate of reform was harshly punished.

sentences.zh: 既下獄，自揣實無罪，謂即訊不難白，次日，遽詔與等同棄市。

translations.literal: After Rui was imprisoned he reckoned himself truly guiltless and thought that once questioned he could easily be cleared; the next day an edict suddenly ordered him executed in the market together with Liu Guangdi and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In prison he believed himself innocent and expected to clear his name at trial; the next day he was executed in the market with the others.

sentences.zh: 改元，子繳手詔於都察院，請代奏，始傳於世。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title, Rui's son Qingchang submitted the emperor's handwritten edict to the Censorate and requested it be memorialized upward; only then did it circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xuantong reign began, his son Qingchang submitted the secret edict to the Censorate for publication, and only then did it become known.

sentences.zh: 劉光第 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Liu Guangdi, style name blank, a man of blank place.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangdi, whose style name was Peicun, was a native of Fushun in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 九年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In 1883 he became a jinshi and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 治事精嚴，因讞獄忤長官​​，遂退而閉戶勤學，絕跡不詣署。

translations.literal: He handled affairs with rigorous precision; because of a capital case he offended his superior, then withdrew, shut his door, studied diligently, and never again set foot in the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: He handled cases with rigorous precision; after offending a superior over a capital case he withdrew, shut himself in to study, and never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 家素貧，而性廉介，非舊交，雖禮饋弗受。

translations.literal: His family had always been poor, yet his nature was incorruptible; except for old friends, even gifts of courtesy he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and he was incorruptible; he accepted no gifts, even courtesy offerings, except from old friends.

sentences.zh: 獨與善。

translations.literal: He alone was on good terms with Yang Rui.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially close to Yang Rui.

sentences.zh: 通、及。

translations.literal: He was versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and the Elder and Younger Dai Commentaries on the Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and the Elder and Younger Dai ritual commentaries.

sentences.zh: 其應召也，亦以薦，然非其素志，將具疏辭，人官京朝者力勸之。

translations.literal: When he was summoned he likewise came on Chen Baozhen's recommendation, yet this was not his lifelong wish; he was about to prepare a memorial declining, but Sichuan men holding capital office strongly urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned on Chen Baozhen's recommendation, though against his inclination; he was about to decline by memorial when fellow Sichuan officials at court pressed him to accept.

sentences.zh: 一日，召見，力陳時危民困，外患日迫，亟宜虛懷圖治，上稱善。

translations.literal: One day on audience he forcefully stated that the times were perilous, the people distressed, foreign peril pressed daily closer, and the throne should urgently open its mind and plan good government; the emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At one audience he urged that with the times perilous, the people suffering, and foreign threat mounting, the throne must open its mind to reform; the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 惟時言路宏啟，臣民奏事日數百計，竟日批答，簽識可否，以待上裁。

translations.literal: Only at that time the memorial channel was broadly opened; officials and commoners submitted affairs by the hundreds each day; Guangdi spent whole days drafting replies, marking approval or rejection, awaiting the emperor's decision.
translations.idiomatic: With the memorial channel wide open, hundreds of submissions arrived daily; he spent whole days drafting replies and marking them for the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 退語所親曰：「吾終不任此，行當亟假歸矣！

translations.literal: On retiring he told those close to him: "I ultimately cannot bear this office; I shall soon urgently take leave and return home!"
translations.idiomatic: He told confidants afterward, "I cannot bear this work; I shall soon take leave and go home!"

sentences.zh: 」未一月而禍作，自投獄。

translations.literal: " Before a month had passed disaster struck; he went of his own accord into prison.
translations.idiomatic: " Within a month disaster struck, and he surrendered himself to prison.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，協辦大學士監斬，詫曰：「未訊而誅，何哉？

translations.literal: At execution Associate Grand Secretary Gangyi supervised the beheading; Guangdi exclaimed in surprise: "Executed without trial — how can this be?"
translations.idiomatic: At the execution Associate Grand Secretary Gangyi supervised; Guangdi exclaimed, "Executed without trial — how can this be?"

sentences.zh: 」令跪聽旨，不可，曰：「祖制，雖盜賊，臨刑呼冤，當復訊。

translations.literal: " He was ordered to kneel and hear the decree; he would not, saying: "By ancestral institution, even for thieves, if at execution they cry out their innocence, there should be reinvestigation."
translations.idiomatic: " Ordered to kneel for the decree, he refused: "By ancestral law, even thieves who cry innocence at execution must be heard again."

sentences.zh: 吾輩縱不足惜，如國體何！

translations.literal: Even if we are not worth sparing, what of the dignity of the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if we are worthless, what of the dignity of the state!"

sentences.zh: 」默不應，再詢之，曰：「吾奉命監刑耳，他何知​​？

translations.literal: " Gangyi was silent and did not answer; asked again, he said: "I am ordered merely to supervise the execution — what else do I know?"
translations.idiomatic: " Gangyi was silent; pressed again, he said, "I am only ordered to supervise the execution — what else do I know?"

sentences.zh: 」獄卒強之跪，崛立自如。

translations.literal: " The jailers forced him to kneel; he stood erect as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Jailers forced him to kneel, but he stood erect.

sentences.zh: 呼曰：「，跪！

translations.literal: Yang Rui called out: "Peicun, kneel!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rui called, "Peicun, kneel!"

sentences.zh: 跪！

translations.literal: Kneel!
translations.idiomatic: Kneel!

sentences.zh: 遵旨而已。

translations.literal: It is only obeying the decree.
translations.idiomatic: Just obey the decree.

sentences.zh: 」乃跪就戮。

translations.literal: " Only then did he kneel and submit to execution.
translations.idiomatic: " Only then did he kneel and die.

sentences.zh: 著有。

translations.literal: His writings include the Jiebai Studio Collected Poems and Prose.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Jiebai Studio Collected Poems and Prose.

sentences.zh: 譚嗣同（唐才常） ，字，人。

translations.literal: Tan Sitong (with Tang Caichang), style name blank, a man of blank place.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Sitong (with Tang Caichang appended), whose style name was Fusheng, was a native of Liuyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父，巡撫。

translations.literal: His father Jixun was governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jixun was governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻有大志，文為奇肆。

translations.literal: In youth he was free-spirited with great ambition; his writing was strange and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and ambitious; his writing was unconventional and forceful.

sentences.zh: 其學以日新為主，視倫常舊說若無足措意者。

translations.literal: His learning took daily renewal as its master and regarded conventional moral teachings as scarcely worth attention.
translations.idiomatic: He took continual renewal as his principle and paid little heed to conventional morality.

sentences.zh: 素謹飭，以是頗見惡。

translations.literal: Jixun had always been cautious and proper, and for this greatly disliked Sitong.
translations.idiomatic: His cautious father Jixun greatly disliked him for this.

sentences.zh: 乃遊幕，以同知入貲為知府，銓。

translations.literal: Sitong then traveled to Liu Jintang's staff in Xinjiang; through subprefect rank purchased with money he became prefect and was assigned to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Liu Jintang's staff in Xinjiang, bought his way to prefect, and was assigned to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 撫，還鄉佐新政。

translations.literal: When Chen Baozhen governed Hunan, Sitong returned home to assist the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Baozhen became Hunan governor, he returned home to help the reforms.

sentences.zh: 倡辦，為之長。

translations.literal: Liang Qichao initiated the Southern Study Society; Sitong became its head.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Qichao founded the Southern Study Society, Sitong became its head.

sentences.zh: 屆會期，集者恆數百人，聞慷慨論時事，多感動。

translations.literal: When meetings convened, those gathered were always several hundred; hearing Sitong speak passionately on current affairs, many were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds gathered at each meeting; his impassioned speeches on current affairs moved many.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，召入都，奏對稱旨，擢四品卿、軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was summoned to the capital; his audience responses pleased the emperor; he was promoted to fourth-rank minister and Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 he was summoned to the capital, pleased the emperor at audience, and was made a fourth-rank minister and Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 四人雖同被命，每召對，建議獨多。

translations.literal: Though the four received the same appointment, at each audience Sitong's proposals were uniquely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Though all four were appointed together, Sitong offered the most proposals at each audience.

sentences.zh: 欲開，設顧問官，令擬旨，必載明前朝故事，將親詣請命太后。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to open the Maojin Hall, establish advisory officials, and order Sitong to draft edicts that must cite clear precedents from former reigns, intending to go in person to the Summer Palace to request the empress dowager's approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to open the Maojin Hall and appoint advisers; Sitong was to draft edicts citing precedents before the emperor went to the Summer Palace for the empress dowager's approval.

sentences.zh: 退謂人曰：「今乃知上絕無權也！

translations.literal: Sitong withdrew and said to others: "Now I know the emperor has absolutely no power!"
translations.idiomatic: He said afterward, "Now I know the emperor has no real power at all!"

sentences.zh: 」時督，以監司練兵。

translations.literal: " At that time Rong Lu governed the metropolitan region; Yuan Shikai as surveillance commissioner trained troops at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong Lu then governed the capital region; Yuan Shikai was training troops at Tianjin as surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔擢侍郎，召入覲。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Yuan Shikai to vice minister and summoned him for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was promoted to vice minister and summoned to audience.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜詣有所議。

translations.literal: Sitong once went by night to Yuan Shikai to discuss matters.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong once visited Yuan Shikai by night for secret talks.

sentences.zh: 明日，返天津。

translations.literal: The next day Yuan returned to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yuan returned to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 越晨，太后自還宮，收政權。

translations.literal: The morning after, the empress dowager returned from the Summer Palace to the Forbidden City and reclaimed political power.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the empress dowager returned from the Summer Palace and seized power back.

sentences.zh: 避匿日本使館，往見之，勸東遊。

translations.literal: Liang Qichao hid in the Japanese legation; Sitong went to see him and urged him to travel east.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qichao hid in the Japanese legation; Sitong visited him and urged him to flee abroad.

sentences.zh: 曰：「不有行者，無以圖將來；

translations.literal: Sitong said: "Without those who go, there is no way to plan for the future;
translations.idiomatic: Sitong said, "Without those who flee, there is no future to plan for;

sentences.zh: 不有死者，無以酬聖主。

translations.literal: without those who die, there is no way to repay the sage ruler."
translations.idiomatic: without those who die, there is no way to repay the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」卒不去。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: " He would not leave.

sentences.zh: 未幾，斬於市。

translations.literal: Before long he was beheaded in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was beheaded in public.

sentences.zh: 著有及等。

translations.literal: His writings include Benevolence Studies and the Mangcang Studio Poetry Collection and others.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Benevolence Studies, the Mangcang Studio Poetry Collection, and other works.

translations.literal: Tang Caichang, style name Fochen.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Caichang, whose style name was Fochen.

sentences.zh: 少與齊名，稱「二生」，高材生也。

translations.literal: In youth he was equally famous with Sitong and was called "the two students of Liuyang"; he was a gifted student of the Two Lakes Academy.
translations.idiomatic: As youths he and Sitong were famed together as "the two students of Liuyang," outstanding pupils of the Two Lakes Academy.

sentences.zh: 聞死，憂憤，屢有所謀，每言及，常泣下。

translations.literal: Hearing of Sitong's death he was grieved and indignant, repeatedly plotted action, and whenever he spoke of the emperor Dezong he often wept.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Sitong's death, he grieved and plotted repeatedly; whenever he spoke of Emperor Guangxu he wept.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，兩宮出狩，陰結謀舉事，號勤王，將攻、。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the two palaces went on tour, he secretly joined the Society of the Rich and plotted an uprising, calling it "loyal service to the throne," intending to attack Wuchang and Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, when the court fled Beijing, he secretly joined the Society of the Rich to raise troops in the name of loyal restoration, planning to attack Wuchang and Hankou.

sentences.zh: 被獲，慷慨言無所隱，請就死，遂殺之。

translations.literal: He was captured, spoke boldly without concealment, asked to accept death, and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Captured, he spoke boldly without reserve, asked to die, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 林旭 ，字，人。

translations.literal: Lin Xu, style name blank, a man of blank place.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xu, whose style name was Dungu, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 年十九，舉本省鄉試第一。

translations.literal: At nineteen he took first place in his province's provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he ranked first in the Fujian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 後試禮部，值構釁，糾同試者上書論時事，不報。

translations.literal: Later he sat for the Ministry of Rites examination; it happened that Sino-Japanese hostilities broke out; he joined fellow candidates in memorializing on current affairs; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: He later took the metropolitan examination; when war with Japan broke out, he joined fellow candidates in a memorial on current affairs that went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 入貲為內閣中書。

translations.literal: He purchased office and became a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He bought his way to a Grand Secretariat secretaryship.

sentences.zh: 時倡言變法，先於京師立，以振厲士氣，而、、、諸會繼之。

translations.literal: At that time Kang Youwei advocated reform; he first established the Cantonese Study Society in the capital to rouse scholarly morale, and the Sichuan, Zhejiang, Shaanxi, and Fujian study societies followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Youwei began advocating reform, he founded the Cantonese Study Society in the capital to stir scholarly morale; Sichuan, Zhejiang, Shaanxi, and Fujian societies followed.

sentences.zh: 為領袖，又充會員。

translations.literal: Xu became leader of the Fujian Study Society and also joined the Society to Protect the State as a member.
translations.idiomatic: Lin led the Fujian Study Society and also joined the Society to Protect the State.

sentences.zh: 先為將軍，雅好士，及至，延入幕。

translations.literal: Rong Lu had earlier been general at Fuzhou and greatly favored Fujian scholars; when he reached Tianjin he took Xu into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu, formerly Fuzhou general and a patron of Fujian scholars, took Lin onto his staff when he went to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 俄以奏保人才召見，操土語，上不盡解。

translations.literal: Soon on memorial recommendation of talent he was summoned for audience; he spoke in his local dialect and the emperor did not fully understand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon recommended as talent, he was summoned to audience; speaking in his Fujian dialect, he was not fully understood.

sentences.zh: 退繕摺，上稱善，遂命與等同參機務，詔諭多起草。

translations.literal: On retiring he drafted a memorial; the emperor praised it and then ordered him to join Tan Sitong and the others in handling confidential affairs; many edicts and instructions were drafted by Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a memorial afterward that the emperor praised; he was ordered to join Tan Sitong and the others in confidential duties, and many edicts were drafted by him.

sentences.zh: 及變起，同戮於市，年二十有四。

translations.literal: When the coup arose he was executed in the market together with the others, aged twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup came he was executed with the others at twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 著有。

translations.literal: His writings include the Late Emerald Studio Poetry Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Late Emerald Studio Poetry Collection.

sentences.zh: 妻孫女，聞變，仰藥不死，以毀卒。

translations.literal: His wife was a granddaughter of Shen Baozhen; hearing of the disaster she took poison but did not die, and died from grief.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, a granddaughter of Shen Baozhen, took poison on hearing the news but survived, then died of grief.

sentences.zh: 康廣仁 ，名，以字行，弟。

translations.literal: Kang Guangren, personal name Youpu, known by his style name, younger brother of Kang Youwei.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Guangren, personal name Youpu, known by his style name, was Kang Youwei's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少從兄學。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under his elder brother from youth.

sentences.zh: 上書請改革，謂當先變科舉，庶人才可出。

translations.literal: When Youwei memorialized requesting reform, Guangren said the examinations should be changed first, so that talent might emerge.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Youwei memorialized for reform, Guangren urged changing the examinations first so talent could emerge.

sentences.zh: 其後罷鄉會試、製藝，而歲科試未變，激勵言官抗疏論之，得旨俞允。

translations.literal: Afterward the provincial and metropolitan examinations and the examination essay were abolished, but the annual provincial tests were not changed; Guangren urged censors to submit defiant memorials on this and received imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: After the provincial and metropolitan exams and the eight-legged essay were abolished, annual tests remained unchanged; he urged censors to protest until the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 於是語：「今科舉既廢，宜且南歸興學專教育，俟養成多數有用才，數年後乃可云改革也。

translations.literal: He then said to Youwei: "Now that the examinations are abolished, you should for the present return south to promote learning and devote yourself to education; wait until many useful talents are cultivated — only after several years can one speak of reform."
translations.idiomatic: He then told Kang Youwei, "With examinations abolished, you should return south to build schools and train talent; only after several years can real reform begin."

sentences.zh: 」不忍去。

translations.literal: " Youwei could not bear to leave.
translations.idiomatic: " Kang Youwei could not bring himself to leave.

sentences.zh: 及初聞變，復趣歸。

translations.literal: When he first heard of the coup, Guangren again urged Youwei to return.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup first broke, he again urged Kang to flee.

sentences.zh: 走，被逮。

translations.literal: Youwei fled; Guangren was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Youwei escaped; Guangren was arrested.

sentences.zh: 在獄言笑自若，臨刑猶言曰：「自強之機在此矣！

translations.literal: In prison he spoke and laughed as if at ease; at execution he still said: "The opportunity for China's self-strengthening lies here!"
translations.idiomatic: In prison he was calm and cheerful; at execution he said, "China's chance to strengthen itself lies in this!"

sentences.zh: 」 【論曰】 論曰：戊戌變法，發憤圖強，用等言，召用新進。

translations.literal: " Commentary says: The Wuxu reforms — Emperor Dezong, roused to strengthen the state, followed the counsel of Li Duanfen and others and summoned newly risen men.
translations.idiomatic: " Commentary: In the 1898 reform movement Emperor Guangxu, determined to strengthen the state, took the advice of Li Duanfen and others and called in a new generation of officials.

sentences.zh: 百日維新，外震仰，黨爭遽起，激成政變。

translations.literal: The Hundred Days of renewal made China and foreign lands look up in awe; factional struggle suddenly arose and provoked the political coup.
translations.idiomatic: The Hundred Days of reform awed China and the world, but factional struggle erupted and triggered the coup.

sentences.zh: 、、、及、同日被禍，世稱「六君子」，皆悲其志。

translations.literal: Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, and Yang Shenxiu and Kang Guangren suffered disaster on the same day; the world calls them "the Six Gentlemen," and all mourn their purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, Yang Shenxiu, and Kang Guangren died on the same day; posterity calls them the Six Gentlemen and mourns their cause.

sentences.zh: 內爭不已，牽及外交。

translations.literal: Internal struggle did not cease and drew in foreign relations.
translations.idiomatic: Internal strife continued and spilled into foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 其後遂釀庚子排外之亂，終致危亡。

translations.literal: Afterward it brewed the gengzi anti-foreign turmoil and in the end brought peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: This led to the anti-foreign Boxer uprising of 1900 and ultimately to national collapse.

sentences.zh: 此亦代興衰一大關鍵也。

translations.literal: This too is a great turning point in the dynasty's rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: This was a decisive turning point in the dynasty's fate.
